Employed to paint glow-in-the-dark watch dials in the 1910s and 1920s, these American factory workers were told to point their brushes with their lips — ingesting a radioactive element that would reshape U.S. labor law. Who were they?
Radium Girls: American female radiation poisoning victims (1917–1978)

This political ideology holds that sovereignty belongs to the people and their elected representatives rather than a hereditary monarch, and champions civic virtue, anti-corruption, and freedom from domination — which ideology?
Republicanism: Political ideology centered on citizenship in a state organized as a republic.
Born in Hong Kong and educated at Eton, this British former diplomat and MP walked solo across Asia after leaving the Foreign Office, and now co-hosts a podcast with Alastair Campbell — who is he?
Rory Stewart: British politician, academic and broadcaster (born 1973)
Venerated as a prophet across three major faiths, this biblical figure guided Israel's transition from the age of judges to kingship, first anointing Saul and later David — who is he?
Rising through the ranks despite the Great Purge of the 1930s, this Soviet officer became a Marshal of the Soviet Union and led the Ukrainian Front during the 1939 invasion of Poland — who is he?

As part of the Battle of the Bulge, this December 1944 clash saw the 101st Airborne help defend a vital Belgian crossroads town where seven main roads converged, blocking the German drive toward Antwerp — which engagement is this?

Siege of Bastogne: American/German engagement December 1944. Until 23 December, the weather prevented Allied aircraft from attempting to resupply Bastogne or from performing ground attack missions against German forces.

Elected king of Poland in 1764 with the backing of Catherine the Great — with whom he'd become intimately involved at the Russian court — he became the last monarch of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; who was he?
Stanisław August Poniatowski: Ruler of Poland–Lithuania from 1764 to 1795.

Ceded by the Qing dynasty after its defeat in an 1895 war with a rising East Asian empire, this island served as that empire's first colony, governed for the next 50 years from a capital called Taihoku — what period of history is this?
Taiwan under Japanese rule: 1895–1945 colony of the Empire of Japan.
He landed at Anzac Cove in 1915, distinguished himself planning the Battle of Pozières, and remains the only Australian ever to reach the rank of field marshal — who was he?

Serving as the eighth U.S. director of national intelligence starting in 2025, this former Hawaii congresswoman deployed to Iraq with the National Guard and later left the Democrats to become a Republican — who is she?
Tulsi Gabbard: American politician and military officer (born 1981)
Serving as the 18th U.S. ambassador to NATO before rising to Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs, this diplomat briefly served as acting deputy secretary of state in 2023 — who is she?
Fought along the Suez Canal from 1967 to 1970 after Arab leaders adopted the 'three no's' policy, this conflict pitted Israel against Egypt, Jordan, and the PLO?
War of Attrition: 1967–1970 war between Israel and Egypt. Following the 1967 Six-Day War, no serious diplomatic efforts were made to resolve the issues at the heart of the Arab–Israeli conflict.

Known as "Old Fuss and Feathers" for his obsession with military etiquette, this veteran of the War of 1812 and the Mexican-American War commanded the U.S. Army for two decades but lost the 1852 election to Franklin Pierce. Who was he?
Winfield Scott: United States Army general (1786–1866)
President of Uganda since 1986, this leader ranks as the third-longest-serving non-royal head of state in the world today — who is he?
Yoweri Museveni: President and dictator of Uganda since 1986. Museveni unified the opposition under the National Resistance Movement and started the Ugandan Bush War.

Which of these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these people was born first?
Jīvaka (born 401 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Giordano Bruno is an astronomer. Bruno's pantheism was not taken lightly by the church, nor was his teaching of metempsychosis regarding the reincarnation of the soul.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Roger Penrose is a mathematician. Sir Roger Penrose (born 8 August 1931) is an English mathematician, mathematical physicist, and philosopher of science.
What is the atomic number of Cadmium?
Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.
What is the atomic number of Lead?
Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb (from the Latin plumbum) and atomic number 82.
In what year was John von Neumann born?
John von Neumann: During World War II, von Neumann worked on the Manhattan Project.
In what year was Manmohan Singh born?
Manmohan Singh: A member of the Indian National Congress, Singh was the first and remains the only Sikh prime minister of India.
In what year was Paracelsus born?
Paracelsus also had a substantial influence as a prophet or diviner, his "Prognostications" being studied by Rosicrucians in the 17th century.
In what year did B. R. Ambedkar die?
B. R. Ambedkar: Ambedkar served as Law and Justice minister in the first cabinet of Jawaharlal Nehru.
In what year did Tomitaro Makino die?
Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year was Pluto discovered?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
TypeScript: Anders Hejlsberg. TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
Pethidine: Pfizer. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.
In which country is Kazan phenomenon?
Kazan phenomenon: Soviet Union. The Kazan mafia was known to be particularly cruel in their extortion tactics, and periodically brought in reinforcements from Tatarstan.
Who is credited with discovering Seaborgium?
Seaborgium: Yuri Oganessian. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen cyanide?
Hydrogen cyanide: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula H−C≡N.
Who is credited with discovering Tungsten?
Tungsten: Juan José Elhuyar. Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
This tsetse-fly-borne parasitic infection, caused by a protozoan, disproportionately affects humans and cattle across Africa — what is it?
Atrocities in the Congo Free State

African trypanosomiasis is an insect-borne parasitic infection of humans and other animals caused by the protozoan species Trypanosoma brucei, which is transmitted by the bite of an infected tsetse fly.
Named after a French physicist considered a father of electromagnetism, this SI unit measures electric current as one coulomb of charge passing a point per second. What unit is it?
Ampere (symbol: A), often shortened to amp, is the unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).
Marked by right lower abdominal pain, nausea, and fever, this common inflammatory condition is typically caused by a blockage from a small hard mass called a fecalith — name the condition?
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
Found throughout North America from Canada to northern Mexico, this sea eagle has two subspecies and forms a pair with the white-tailed eagle—name it.
Bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America.
Present in every living cell and abundant in liver and meats, this B vitamin acts as an enzyme cofactor and takes its name from the Greek for 'life' — what is it?
Biotin (also known as vitamin B7 and vitamin H) is one of the B vitamins - a group of essential dietary micronutrients.
This American actor played Kyle Parks on Lifetime's The Client List before joining the cast of Revenge as Ben Hunter — who is he?
Brian Hallisay (born October 31, 1978) is an American actor, known for his roles as Will Davis in The CW drama series Privileged and Kyle Parks in the Lifetime drama series The Client List.
Nine to ten times as massive as the Sun and expanded to 71 times its radius, this blue-loop giant in the constellation Carina ranks second only to Sirius in night-sky brightness — which star?
Canopus is the brightest star in the southern constellation of Carina and the second-brightest star in the night sky.
Built under license from the Soviet MiG-21, this Chinese fighter jet carries the NATO reporting name Fishcan and specializes in short-range air combat — what aircraft is it?
Chengdu J-7 (pinyin: Jin-7; third generation export version J-7; NATO reporting name: Fishcan) is a Chinese fighter aircraft.
A scale insect native to tropical and subtropical parts of the Americas that lives on prickly-pear cacti, this parasite is the source of the natural dye carmine — which insect?
Cochineal (-eel, US also, -eel; Dactylopius coccus) is a scale insect in the suborder Sternorrhyncha, from which the natural dye carmine is derived.

Though Colin Maclaurin published special cases two years earlier, this determinant-based method for solving linear systems bears the name of the mathematician who generalized it in 1750 — what's it known as?
Cramer's rule is an explicit formula for the solution of a system of linear equations with as many equations as unknowns, valid whenever the system has a unique solution.
Caused by either too little insulin or cells that ignore it, this condition keeps blood sugar stubbornly high and comes chiefly in a type 1 and a type 2 — what is it?
Diabetes is a group of common endocrine diseases characterized by sustained high blood sugar levels.
Which natural science examines how living things relate to their environment, spanning the individual, population, community, ecosystem, and biosphere levels?
Ecology (from Ancient Greek (okos) 'house' and - (-loga) 'study of') is the natural science of the relationships among living organisms and their environment.

Discovered in January 2005 by a Palomar Observatory team and named after a Greco-Roman goddess of strife, this trans-Neptunian object is the most massive known dwarf planet in the solar system — which one?
Eris (dwarf planet) (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
This field of study, related to economics and business administration, is typically divided into personal, corporate, and public branches. What field is it?
Finance refers to monetary resources as well as the discipline that studies such resources, with related concepts such as money, currency, assets and liabilities.
This scholarly discipline covers the link between food and culture, from recipes and regional cooking styles to the rigorous science of good eating — what's it called?

Gastronomy is the study of the relationship between food and culture, the art of preparing and serving rich or delicate and appetizing food, the cooking styles of particular regions, and the science of good eating.
A friar, mathematician, and meteorologist who quietly worked out the laws of heredity with garden peas — and only got credit long after his death — who was this founder of genetics?
Gregor Mendel (20 July 1822 - 6 January 1884) was an Austrian biologist, meteorologist, mathematician, Augustinian friar and abbot of St.
This discipline governs the design and formal description ('blazon') of coats of arms, crests, and other armorial bearings — what is it called?
Heraldry (also known as armoury) is a discipline relating to the design, display, study and transmission of armorial bearings.

This altered mental state involves intensely focused attention, reduced awareness of surroundings, and heightened responsiveness to suggestion, though scientists still debate whether it's truly a distinct state of consciousness — what is it?

Hypnosis is a human condition involving focused attention (the selective attention/selective inattention hypothesis, SASI), reduced peripheral awareness, and an enhanced capacity to respond to suggestion.

In 1897, this British physicist showed that cathode rays were made of previously unknown negatively charged particles far smaller than atoms — the first subatomic particle ever identified. Who was he?
J. J. Thomson (18 December 1856 - 30 August 1940) was a British physicist.

After leaving the company where he led industrial design for decades, this British-American designer founded the creative collective LoveFrom, which now works with Ferrari, Airbnb, and OpenAI. Who is he?
Jony Ive (born 27 February 1967) is a British-American designer.
Originally a water-retrieving gun dog from Italy's Po Delta marshes, this breed later became prized for hunting truffles once its wetland habitat was drained — what breed is it?
Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian breed of dog.

The second woman to earn a physics doctorate from the University of Vienna, this Austrian-Swedish scientist became the first female full physics professor in Germany — and was instrumental in discovering nuclear fission. Who is she?
Lise Meitner (7 November 1878 - 27 October 1968) was an Austrian and Swedish nuclear physicist who was instrumental in the discovery of nuclear fission.

Made by every living organism and responsible for much of the sour taste in fruit, this dicarboxylic food additive's salt form also serves as a key intermediate in the cell's central metabolic energy cycle — what compound is it?
Malic acid is an organic compound with the molecular formula HO2CCH(OH)CH2CO2H.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.

Native to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, with one invasive species now in the southern U.S., this reptile genus ranges from 20 centimeters long to over 3 meters in the Komodo dragon — name this group of lizards?
Monitor lizard are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.

Sometimes reaching two meters long but often thinner than a millimeter or two wide, these thread-like parasitoid worms turn up in damp puddles, troughs, and swimming pools as adults — what phylum is this?

Nematomorpha (sometimes called Gordiacea, and commonly known as horsehair worms, hairsnakes, or Gordian worms) are a phylum of parasitoid animals similar to yet distinct from nematode worms in morphology, hence the name.
Many species in this bird family scavenge alongside pigeons and gulls, while two of its city-dwelling members are famous for nesting directly on buildings — which family are they?
Old World sparrow are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Making up the order Psittaciformes, these birds are known for a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet, with a third of all species threatened by extinction — name the group?
Parrot (order Psittaciformes), also known as psittacines from the name of the type genus Psittacus, are birds with a strong curved beak, upright stance, and clawed feet.
Made in the body from the amino acid L-phenylalanine, this natural stimulant also turns up in fermented chocolate and inhibits a transporter called VMAT2 — what is it?
Phenethylamine (PEA) is an organic compound, natural monoamine alkaloid, and trace amine, which acts as a central nervous system stimulant in humans.
It looks like a single point of light, but this brightest star of Ursa Minor is actually a triple star system parked near the north celestial pole — what is it?
Polaris is a yellow supergiant star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Minor.

This sympathomimetic medication is best known as a nasal decongestant, though at higher doses it can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant, making it a common drug of abuse — what's the compound called?
Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
First flown in 1955 as a nuclear-strike follow-on to the Mach 1 Super Sabre, this fighter-bomber earned the nickname 'Thud' and flew most early Vietnam War strike missions — which aircraft?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief is an American fighter-bomber that served with the United States Air Force from 1958 to 1984.
One of the world's oldest crops, this thistle-like annual plant with globular orange or red flower heads is grown commercially today for oil pressed from its seeds — what is it?
Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
About 90% of the body's supply of this mood-regulating monoamine is actually made in the gut, where it helps drive intestinal movements — which neurotransmitter is it?
Serotonin (5-HT), is a monoamine neurotransmitter with a wide range of functions in both the central nervous system (CNS) and also peripheral tissues.
Known by such nicknames as 'sour dock' and 'spinach dock,' this tangy Eurasian herb thrives wild in grasslands and is often used as a leaf vegetable — which plant?
Sorrel (Rumex acetosa) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family Polygonaceae.
The fifth most common element on Earth, this multivalent nonmetal usually turns up in sulfide and sulfate minerals and is a bright yellow crystalline solid — what is it?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
Discovered independently by two chemists in 1861 via its distinctive green spectral line, this silvery-white metal takes its name from the Greek word for a green shoot or twig — what element is it?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
Taken by mouth, injection, or inhalation, this steroid helps prevent asthma and COPD flare-ups from worsening — which medication?
Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
This southwestern European viper's bite can be more dangerous than the common adder's — up to 4% of untreated cases are fatal — which species?
Vipera aspis is a viper species found in southwestern Europe.
Passed only from fathers to sons, this genetic structure carries the SRY gene that typically triggers development of male gonads in mammals — what is it?
Y chromosome is one of two sex chromosomes in therian mammals and other organisms.
Genetic in roughly 80% of cases, this long-term skin condition clogs hair follicles with dead skin and sebum, producing blackheads and pimples on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne: Skin condition characterized by pimples.

German-born theoretical physicist celebrated for E=mc² and work on relativity — he won the 1921 Nobel Prize not for those breakthroughs, but for discovering the photoelectric effect. Who revolutionized physics across multiple domains?
Commonly called buffalo, this large grazing mammal endemic to North America is one of just two living species in its genus, alongside a European cousin — what animal is it?
American bison: Species of bovid artiodactyl mammal.

Characterized by extreme food restriction and a fear of gaining weight despite being underweight, this eating disorder is described in the DSM-5 as involving a disturbance in how one perceives their own body shape — what's the condition called?
Anorexia nervosa: Eating disorder. Individuals with anorexia nervosa have a fear of gaining weight, despite the fact that they are typically underweight.
The third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere at nearly 1%, this noble gas takes its name from an Ancient Greek word meaning 'lazy' or 'inactive' — what element is it?
Argon: Chemical element with atomic number 18 (Ar)
From the Greek for "self-devouring," this lysosome-driven process lets a cell tidily break down and recycle its own worn-out parts — what is it?
Autophagy: Process of cells digesting parts of themselves.
Spurred by the 1980 failure of Operation Eagle Claw, this American tiltrotor blends a helicopter's vertical takeoff with a turboprop's long-range cruise — what aircraft is it?
Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey: Military transport tiltrotor.

A French child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, then built one of the first mechanical calculators and traded letters with Fermat that helped birth probability theory — who was he?
Typically housed in the head near the organs for vision, hearing, and smell, this organ processes thought and cognition while coordinating muscle activity — which organ?
Brain: Organ central to the nervous system.
Native to the Americas from Patagonia to western Canada, members of this succulent plant family thrive in the bone-dry Atacama Desert — what are they?
Cactus: Family of mostly succulent plants, adapted to dry environments.

A German child prodigy turned director of the Göttingen Observatory, this mathematician, astronomer, and physicist made landmark contributions across number theory, algebra, statistics, and probability — who is he?
Carl Friedrich Gauss: German polymath and scholar (1777–1855)
This Italian physician who died in 1909 is considered the founder of modern criminology, arguing that 'born criminals' could be spotted by physical defects — who is he?
Add this steely-grey transition metal (atomic number 24) to steel and you get stainless; polish it and it reflects nearly 70% of visible light without tarnishing. Which element is it?
Chromium: Chemical element with atomic number 24 (Cr)
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy, this opiate is a prodrug of morphine often paired with paracetamol to treat mild pain, coughs, and even diarrhea — what is it?
Codeine: Opiate and prodrug of morphine used to treat pain. It usually starts working after half an hour, with maximum effect at two hours.
Caused by a fungus that forms galls on maize plants, this disease produces an edible delicacy in Mexico known as huitlacoche, often stuffed into quesadillas — which condition?
Corn smut: Fungal plant disease on maize and teosinte.
Its Greek name literally means 'boat beard,' describing how its hairy spikelets project from boat-shaped sheaths — better known by a common name evoking a citrus scent, what is this grass genus?
First patented in Germany in 1920 and later synthesized by an American chemist in 1932, this semi-synthetic opioid is roughly ten times more potent than morphine — what is it called?
Desomorphine: Semi-synthetic opioid, morphine analogue. It was first discovered and patented in Germany by a German team working for Knoll in 1920 but was not generally recognized.
Despite its common names, this evergreen conifer isn't a true member of the pine, spruce, or hemlock genera, yet stands as the tallest species in its own family — what is it?
Douglas fir: Species of tree. It is native to western North America and is also known as Douglas-fir, Douglas spruce, Oregon pine, and Columbian pine.

A subfield of physics and electrical engineering, this discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify current — and to convert AC to DC or analog to digital — what is it?

Electronics: Branch of physics and electrical engineering. The semiconductor industry is one of the global economy's largest and most profitable industries, with annual revenues exceeding $481 billion in 2018.
About 60 to 70 percent as sweet as table sugar yet virtually calorie-free, this sugar alcohol is fermented from corn and was commercially pioneered by Japanese companies in the 1990s — what is it?
Erythritol: Sugar alcohol that is used as a sweetener.
Sporting a dark facial mask and famous for a seriously foul-smelling territorial secretion, this stocky mustelid ranges across the continent and Morocco's Rif mountains — which species is it?
Found on the forelimbs of most tetrapods, these prehensile, often opposable digits give primates like humans their dexterity for grasping and fine movement — what are they called?

This German chemist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a process that synthesizes ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen gas — a breakthrough that today supports nearly half the world's food production. Who is he?

A Belgian Catholic priest and physicist, he was first to argue that the recession of galaxies proves an expanding universe, and proposed a 'primeval atom' — the first version of the Big Bang theory. Who was he?
Georges Lemaître: Belgian scientist and Catholic priest (1894–1966)
A U.S. Navy rear admiral who helped develop COBOL, this computer science pioneer wrote what's considered the first computer manual and worked on the Harvard Mark I — who is she?
Grace Hopper: U.S. naval officer and computer scientist (1906–1992)

Coined by psychologist Edward Thorndike, this cognitive bias describes how a positive impression in one area, like someone's looks, skews our judgment of them in unrelated areas — what is this bias called?
Halo effect: Tendency for positive impressions to contaminate other evaluations.

Synthesized from the dried latex of the opium poppy, this opioid is used medically in some countries to relieve pain during childbirth or a heart attack — and its 'black tar' form is a crude, variable mix of morphine derivatives — what is it?
Heroin: Opioid analgesic and recreational drug.
The flowers of this shrub genus act as natural pH indicators, turning blue in acidic soil and pink in alkaline soil?
Powered by four underperforming Lyulka turbojets, this aircraft became the first Soviet jet bomber to fly before being cancelled in September 1947 — which plane?
Ilyushin Il-22: 1947 Soviet bomber aircraft prototype. The Ilyushin Il-22, USAF/DOD designation Type 10, was the first Soviet jet-engined bomber to fly.
As president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995, this French politician spearheaded the creation of the single market and laid the groundwork for the euro — who is he?
A real estate magnate and Spanish–American War officer worth roughly $87 million, he was the richest passenger aboard the Titanic — and went down with it in 1912. Who was he?
John Jacob Astor IV: American businessman and Titanic passenger (1864–1912)
This German-Finnish internet entrepreneur founded the file-hosting service Megaupload before U.S. authorities seized it in 2012 — who is he?
Soft, dense, and bluish-silver when freshly cut, this heavy metal carries the highest atomic number of any stable element — and its Latin name, plumbum, gives it the symbol Pb. Which element is it?
Lead: Chemical element with atomic number 82 (Pb)
Understood before 1950 purely as the ability to decode written words, this concept later expanded to include the social and cultural dimensions of reading and writing — what skill is it?
Literacy: Ability to read and write.
Encoded by the codons AAA and AAG, this basic, essential amino acid cannot be synthesized by the human body — which one is it?
Lysine: Amino acid. Lysine (symbol Lys or K) is an α-amino acid that is a precursor to many proteins.

The first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the first person to win two, this Polish-born physicist and chemist discovered revolutionary elements and shared groundbreaking research on radioactivity with her husband—making her one of history's most influential scientists. Who was she?
Marie Curie: Polish-French physicist and chemist (1867–1934)
Nicknamed 'meow meow' and chemically related to compounds in the khat plant, this synthetic stimulant produces effects similar to MDMA and was first synthesized in 1929 — which drug?
Mephedrone: Recreational drug. Mephedrone, also known as 4-methylmethcathinone, 4-MMC, or 4-methylephedrone, is a synthetic stimulant drug belonging to the amphetamine and cathinone classes.
Soviet pilots nicknamed this 1972 gunship the 'flying tank,' a helicopter NATO calls 'Hind' that can also haul eight troops and still flies in 52 countries. What is it?
Mil Mi-24: Family of assault and attack helicopters.
Numbering roughly 160,000 species and mostly active at night, these insects share an order with butterflies but are known for their duller, darker wings — what are they?
Moth: Group of mostly-nocturnal insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Also called the belly button, this flat or hollowed spot on the abdomen marks where the umbilical cord once attached — what is it?
Navel: Scarred area on the abdomen after detachment of the umbilical cord.

The first of the Century Series jet fighters, this supersonic aircraft was the U.S. Air Force's first fighter capable of level supersonic flight, first taking to the air in May 1953, seven months ahead of schedule — which jet?

North American F-100 Super Sabre: 1953 fighter aircraft family. The North American F-100 Super Sabre is an American supersonic jet fighter aircraft designed and produced by the aircraft manufacturer North American Aviation.
Named after an ancient Greek city, this cactus genus is better known by its fruit's common name, the prickly pear, and goes by nopal or sabra in other cultures — what genus is it?
Opuntia: Genus of cactus. The plant has been introduced to Australia, southern Europe, the Middle East, and parts of Africa.

Named after the bones that house them — frontal, maxillary, ethmoid, and sphenoid — these four paired air-filled spaces surround the nasal cavity and have a still-debated evolutionary purpose — what are they called?
Paranasal sinuses: Air-filled spaces surrounding the nasal cavity.
This nerve-damage condition can be triggered by diabetes, vitamin B12 deficiency, or certain chemotherapy and antibiotic drugs, and may come on suddenly or creep in slowly — what is it?
Peripheral neuropathy: Nervous system disease affecting nerves beyond the brain and spinal cord.
Boasting the longest cones of any spruce and widely planted as a Christmas tree, this European conifer was also the first gymnosperm to have its genome sequenced — which species?
Picea abies: Species of plant. Picea abies, the Norway spruce, Norway fir or European spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.
Born Joseph Ratzinger, this head of the Catholic Church made history in 2013 by resigning the role, then adopted the title 'emeritus' until his death — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI: Head of the Catholic Church from 2005 to 2013.

With 348 known species spanning an opportunistic human pathogen, a plant disease-causer, and a soil-dwelling growth-promoter, which gram-negative bacterial genus in Gammaproteobacteria is renowned for its metabolic diversity?
Pseudomonas: Genus of Gram-negative bacteria. Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
This Norwegian shared the very first Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics, and we owe him the words 'econometrics,' 'microeconomics,' and 'macroeconomics' — who was he?
Ragnar Frisch: Norwegian economist and Nobel Laureate (1895–1973)
Native to Europe, northwestern Africa, and southwestern Asia, this flowering shrub's edible fruit stars in desserts and preserves — what's its species name, better known as the gooseberry?
Ribes uva-crispa: Species of flowering plant in the family Grossulariaceae.
Introduced in the 1970s, this database language let programmers grab many records with one single command, eliminating the need to specify an index path to reach each one — what is it?

Originally from the Mediterranean, this yellowish-gray arthropod has up to 15 pairs of long legs and preys on insects with venom too mild to harm humans — what species commonly invades homes worldwide?
Scutigera coleoptrata: Species of arthropod. Scutigera coleoptrata, also known as the house centipede, is a species of centipede that is typically yellowish-gray and has up to 15 pairs of long legs.
Named after a Native American war chief, this four-blade, twin-engine Army helicopter entered service in 1979 to replace the Bell UH-1 Iroquois — which aircraft is it?
Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk: Series of military utility transport helicopters.

Found in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and northeastern Australia, this large flightless black bird is a close ratite relative of the emu and ostrich, and its Australian population is listed as endangered — which bird?
Southern cassowary: Species of flightless bird. It is one of the three living species of cassowary, alongside the dwarf cassowary and the northern cassowary.
This throat infection causes fever, red tonsils, and swollen neck glands, and can trigger a sandpaper-textured rash known as scarlet fever — which condition?
Streptococcal pharyngitis: Medical condition. It may be spread directly through touching infected sores.
The lone species in its genus, this African-born leguminous tree gives pods of sweet-tangy pulp used in cuisines worldwide, plus a seed oil and even a dye — what is it?
Tamarind: Leguminous tree bearing edible fruit.
